one_line: AI-assisted multi-city travel planning with flight, hotel, weather, and itinerary tools.
what_it_does: Plans multi-city trips by combining flight and hotel search, weather-aware packing advice, travel guides, and saved trip state.
leverage_rationale: The claimed 11 typed tools cover a multi-step travel lifecycle and could reduce orchestration friction, but the packet provides no live agent or video evidence and the same searches can largely be performed through ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT TEXT claims 11 WebMCP tools spanning search, selection, booking preparation, saving, cart, and travel guide.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows a multi-city itinerary form, but not agent interaction.
execution_rationale: The screenshot supports a coherent multi-city search form, while search results, hotel/weather flows, and end-to-end planning are not demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows Paris, Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka destinations with dates, travelers, class, and Search.
FACTS report no submitted video.
impact_rationale: Multi-city travel research is a clear, burdensome use case with a plausible audience; the packet supports the planning premise but not the full solution quality.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT identifies the burden of coordinating flights, hotels, weather, packing, and activities.
Visible itinerary form matches the stated audience need.
creativity_rationale: Combining travel planning and agent orchestration is a useful synthesis, though not a highly novel interaction model from the evidence.
creativity_evidence: PITCH combines multi-city planning with weather-aware packing and browser-agent collaboration.
usability_note: The visible multi-city form is understandable; broader workflow usability is unclear.
red_flags: No video or frame evidence; core claimed flows are not visibly verified.
Demo is reported alive, but packet does not show live behavior.
standouts: Clear multi-city travel workflow and structured lifecycle tool concept.
advance_reason: Plausible product and impact, but thin evidence and unverified WebMCP leverage do not support advancing over demonstrated entries.

one_line: A browser agent turns natural-language board-game variations into safe playable games.
what_it_does: Uses a rule-defined modular game framework to create, edit, test, publish, and play board-game variants with bots and multiplayer.
leverage_rationale: The product is centered on an agent safely manipulating shared structured game rules, testing them with fast bots, and producing a playable result without writing code; this is materially beyond generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: TRANSCRIPT describes natural-language rule changes, live shared progress, interjection, validation, bot search, and multiplayer publication.
ABOUT TEXT says rules are data rather than arbitrary code so agents can safely validate and search them.
Frame sheets visibly show editor, asset library, changing game-piece arrangements, and preview states.
execution_rationale: The long demo transcript and frame sheets show a coherent edit-test-play workflow with manual override, bots, and rule changes; some final multiplayer/publication claims are not directly visible.
execution_evidence: 196-second video transcript covers creation, live preview, bot validation, manual edits, replay, and publication.
Frame sheets show repeated configuration, asset selection, and changing previews.
Devpost screenshot visibly presents the rock-paper-scissors Tic-Tac-Toe concept.
impact_rationale: Variant-game designers and players have a concrete need to test whether novel rules are fun; immediate safe play and bot evaluation address that need directly.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT identifies the repeated deploy-cycle problem for board-game variants.
PITCH targets turning an idea into a playable online multiplayer game.
Transcript shows the creator playing the resulting variant against a bot.
creativity_rationale: The combination of natural-language rule design, data-only safe execution, high-speed bot search, and immediate playable multiplayer output is a memorable and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Rule-defined rather than code-defined games enable safe agent-authored variants.
Transcript demonstrates changing Tic-Tac-Toe to rock-paper-scissors and then changing win conditions.
usability_note: The described interject/pause/manual-editor flow is user-centered; the frame text is small but the editor-preview structure is clear.
red_flags: Frame sheets are low resolution, so exact controls cannot be verified visually.
standouts: Agent-human co-editing plus bot validation and immediate play.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP-centered interaction with strong demonstrated workflow, clear audience value, and unusual ambition.

one_line: A synthetic security proving ground enforcing human approval and replayable evidence for agent actions.
what_it_does: Admits bounded scenarios, simulates deterministic decisions, requests human approval, applies and verifies synthetic effects, compensates them, and exports evidence.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the governed stateful interface: tools contract after simulation so the agent cannot approve its own action, while human approval and replayable receipts remain authoritative.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT TEXT specifies state-shaped tools and removal of approval authority from the agent.
Screenshot visibly shows the synthetic-only claim boundary and staged agent/human workflow.
FACTS include three submitted frame sheets, though files were unavailable at the supplied paths.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a detailed deterministic lifecycle and fixed-seed scenarios with strong coherence, but no accessible frame sheets and no video transcript reduce end-to-end verification.
execution_evidence: ABOUT TEXT describes validator, decision engine, approval gate, effect, receipt, compensation, and evidence digest.
Devpost screenshot visibly presents the cyber-defense dungeon and workflow stages.
impact_rationale: Security teams and agent-platform builders have a serious need for bounded, observable approval workflows; synthetic scope makes the value credible as a test and governance tool.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT identifies the dangerous detection-to-action autonomy boundary.
Screenshot states SYNTHETIC_SIMULATION_ONLY and shows human approval before effect.
creativity_rationale: The progressive capability contraction and proof/compensation lifecycle is an original, ambitious framing for testing agent security boundaries.
creativity_evidence: Three fixed-seed scenarios and judge-authored packs are described.
No-agent-approval boundary is explicit in both text and screenshot.
usability_note: The staged workflow and mobile-oriented UI appear understandable, though live interaction is not verified here.
red_flags: Referenced frame sheets were not present at the exact supplied paths, preventing direct inspection.
standouts: Replayable evidence and compensation rather than merely blocking actions.
advance_reason: High WebMCP leverage and important, unusually well-specified security workflow despite incomplete visual evidence.

one_line: A browser-local file workbench for editing PDFs, images, video, and audio without uploading content.
what_it_does: Lets users and agents inspect and transform local media through 29 state-shaped tools while returning metadata/facts rather than sensitive file contents.
leverage_rationale: Privacy-preserving structured tools let an agent perform useful local transformations and redaction without receiving file contents, a meaningful capability change versus UI automation.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT TEXT claims tools return facts and redaction match locations, never sensitive contents.
ABOUT TEXT describes shared state, worker processing, vendored dependencies, and CSP blocking uploads.
Frame sheet visibly shows empty-to-file-library progression and local-first messaging.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent local file workbench and documented redaction design, but exact edit outputs and all media types are not visibly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet visibly shows local-files message, file categories, and populated file view.
ABOUT TEXT gives specific PDF flattening/redaction behavior and state-dependent tool counts.
impact_rationale: People handling sensitive documents and media have a concrete privacy need; local processing and content-hiding agent results directly address it.
impact_evidence: PITCH explicitly promises content is not uploaded.
ABOUT TEXT explains redacting bank-account matches without exposing numbers.
creativity_rationale: An agent editing content it is deliberately forbidden to read is a strong and memorable privacy-oriented interaction concept, pursued across multiple media types.
creativity_evidence: Content-blind local redaction is explicitly described.
29 tools span PDF, photo, video, and audio workflows.
usability_note: Every tool has a button and the interface progresses from empty bench to file view; details are small in the frame sheet.
red_flags: No transcript and frame sheet labels are mostly unreadable.
Claims of broad media support are not individually demonstrated.
advance_reason: Meaningful WebMCP/privacy innovation with credible audience value and coherent evidence.

one_line: A video editing studio where a director and agent share revision-aware project state.
what_it_does: Provides scripts, scenes, assets, preview, timeline, checkpoints, bounded edits, history, and structural quality checks for human-agent video production.
leverage_rationale: Semantic tools operate on authoritative shared project state with locks, revisions, checkpoints, and bounded operations; this is substantially more reliable than pixel-driving an editor.

execution_evidence: ABOUT TEXT describes project context, selection, edits, checkpoints, ledger, and structural checks.

impact_rationale: Video directors and editors can benefit from bounded assistance that preserves authorship and reversibility, though the submitted scope is more studio workflow than finished production output.
impact_evidence: PITCH explicitly targets director-agent collaboration.

creativity_rationale: Human-directed non-linear editing with visible agent ledger and checkpoint restoration is a fresh synthesis, though the underlying editor category is established.
creativity_evidence: Agent changes appear in a ledger and can be restored without leaving the editor.
usability_note: Revision and checkpoint affordances suggest good control, but no visual workflow evidence was accessible.
red_flags: No video or gallery images despite frame-sheet references.
Live media generation and rendering are disabled.
standouts: Revision-aware bounded collaboration and reversible checkpoints.
advance_reason: Promising architecture, but insufficient packet evidence to substantiate execution at this stage.

one_line: A browser-local 3D editor that turns references into printable, validated custom keycaps.
what_it_does: Generates or imports 3D parts locally, places and composes them on keycaps, repairs printability, validates solids, and exports only after user approval.
leverage_rationale: Typed semantic modeling tools expose transforms, previews, manufacturing composition, validation, and approval over shared live 3D state, avoiding brittle coordinate automation.
leverage_evidence: TRANSCRIPT names find parts, repair printability, autoplace, compose, render union, validate, and export tools.

execution_rationale: The video transcript gives unusually complete end-to-end evidence from local reconstruction through placement, repair, solid validation, and approved STL export, with a coherent direct-manipulation fallback.
execution_evidence: 134-second transcript reports 75,212-triangle model correction, 8-mm normalization, placement, repair preview, union, watertight validation, and approval-gated export.
ABOUT TEXT lists key sizes, mounts, editable transforms, section views, and tolerance coupon.
Devpost screenshot is packaging only; video is the main evidence.
impact_rationale: Makers who want personalized printable keycaps face real modeling and printability barriers; this product addresses the full path from idea to manufacturable file.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT enumerates disconnected skills and the practical printability gap.
Transcript demonstrates exact dimensions, manifold validation, and final STL approval.
creativity_rationale: Combining browser-local image-to-3D, semantic agent collaboration, CAD-like editing, manufacturing validation, and reversible human approval is highly ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Browser-local TripoSR plus printable keycap composition.

usability_note: Direct manipulation, previews, undo, and approval gates provide a strong human-control model; local model download may add friction.
red_flags: Model download time is acknowledged, though demo time-lapses it.
standouts: End-to-end printable artifact rather than a visual-only 3D demo.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: demonstrated end-to-end execution, high user value, and WebMCP materially improving complex 3D editing.

what_it_does: Collects evidence-bound candidate conclusions, runs deterministic checks, routes human approval, preserves lineage, and exposes scoped retrieval to successor agents.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes product semantics for evidence, lineage, checks, policy, and agent access while preserving the human approval boundary; this is more reliable than UI navigation for governance work.

one_line: A floor-plan editor where agents measure accessibility and propose geometry fixes.
what_it_does: Lets humans draw plans while an agent checks wheelchair/walking-frame routes, identifies dimensional failures, and proposes approval-gated layout changes.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent a real geometry engine and structured measurements, enabling reliable spatial checks and bounded edits that image/UI reasoning cannot reproduce comparably well.
leverage_evidence: TRANSCRIPT shows the agent checking wheelchair access and walking distance without user interaction, then proposing door and kitchen changes.
ABOUT TEXT emphasizes geometry engine, route narrowing, thresholds, and turning circles.
Video frame sheets submitted per FACTS.
execution_rationale: The 173-second video transcript demonstrates a complete inspect-diagnose-propose-approve workflow with concrete dimensions and visible plan changes.
execution_evidence: Transcript reports 760-mm clear opening versus 815-mm need, unreachable bathroom, kitchen turning-circle warning, proposed fixes, and approval.
PITCH and ABOUT TEXT consistently describe human drawing/agent measurement separation.
impact_rationale: People adapting homes, carers, and small landlords have a concrete accessibility problem where geometric errors can materially harm daily life; the demonstrated checks directly address it.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT names injury adaptation, carers, and landlords as audiences.
Transcript demonstrates identifying a wheelchair-inaccessible bathroom and proposing corrective geometry.
creativity_rationale: The human-draws/agent-measures interaction is a fresh and disciplined use of WebMCP, with practical spatial simulation rather than generic generation.
creativity_evidence: Agent sends wheelchair and walking-frame tests through the geometry engine.
Approval-gated edits preserve human design authority.
usability_note: Clear separation between drawing, automated checks, and explicit approval; exact UI details are secondary to the strong demonstrated flow.
standouts: Concrete accessibility impact backed by dimensional evidence.
advance_reason: High-value, clearly demonstrated human-agent workflow where structured WebMCP measurement is central rather than decorative.

one_line: Learns typed agent tools from human demonstrations while enforcing physical approval for risky actions.
what_it_does: Synthesizes parameterized WebMCP tools from demonstrations, assigns risk and provenance, quarantines untrusted content, and gates irreversible commits with WebAuthn and audit logs.
leverage_rationale: Deputy changes both how capabilities are authored and how they execute: semantic tools are learned from work, while exact-argument human passkey approval makes dangerous consent unavailable to the agent.
leverage_evidence: TRANSCRIPT demonstrates creating a customer and invoice, synthesizing a tool, then blocking a refund behind a passkey.
ABOUT TEXT specifies digest-bound WebAuthn, single-use commit registration, quarantine, and hash-chained audit.
Frame sheets submitted per FACTS.
execution_rationale: The video transcript presents a coherent demonstration-to-tool-to-risk-gate flow and the technical description is unusually specific; some claims such as tamper-proof details are not independently observable.
execution_evidence: 190-second transcript covers demonstration, inferred schema/risk, risky refund refusal, passkey layer, quarantine, and audit log.
ABOUT TEXT gives canonical digest binding and single-use commit mechanics.
impact_rationale: Agent safety, human consent, and no-code capability authoring address pressing needs for businesses exposing consequential web actions to agents.
impact_evidence: ABOUT TEXT identifies self-approved agent actions as the problem.
Transcript shows payment/refund action blocked until human physical approval.
creativity_rationale: Learning agent capabilities from ordinary human work while cryptographically binding irreversible approval to exact tool/version/arguments is highly original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Human demonstration synthesizes a typed tool without coding.
Quarantine boundary treats external text as data rather than commands.
usability_note: No-code demonstration authoring and structured refusal are promising; passkey setup is an unavoidable adoption friction.
red_flags: Transcript says some security layers are still being added, suggesting portions may be in-progress.
standouts: Physical human approval cannot be forged by clicking the page.
advance_reason: Highly consequential and novel agent-infrastructure concept with strong demonstrated workflow and exceptionally high WebMCP leverage.
